docs.title: lensml
docs.text:
The AI agent that supervises your ML training runs.

lensml is a Python package + local web dashboard that watches your PyTorch training run in real time, detects pathologies as they emerge (exploding gradients, dead ReLUs, missing input normalization, …), proposes a libcst-level patch, commits it to a session branch on your approval, and resumes from the last checkpoint with the fixed code.

The pitch in one sentence: "integration, not invention" — every piece of the pipeline already exists; lensml is the open-source agent that wires them together.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
pip install "git+https://github.com/rupeshbharambe24/lensml.git"   # not on PyPI yet
lensml dashboard &        # http://localhost:8000
# in your training script:
import lensml
lensml.watch(model, optimizer)

docs.title: lensml-bench
docs.text: A reproducibility benchmark for the v1 detector and fix-template catalogue (plan §6).

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
lensml/bench/
  fixtures.py           Fixture loader + meta.json validator
  grader.py             run_script + grade_script + apply_diff
  runner.py             BenchRunner: run_one + run_all + JSON cache
  baseline.py           BaselineRunner (LLM-only baseline arm)
  report.py             Markdown + JSON report renderer
  fixtures/
    tiny/<class>/<idx>/
      bug.py            broken training script
      fix.diff          canonical unified diff
      grade.py          grader entry-point shim
      meta.json         {pathology_class, difficulty, host_env, max_steps,
                         loss_threshold, metric_threshold?, metric_name?}

docs.title: Three-check protocol (plan §6.1)
docs.text:
1. Runs — does the (patched) script exit 0?
  2. Loss converged — does final_loss <= meta.loss_threshold?
  3. Metric passed — when meta.metric_threshold is set, does final_metric >= threshold?

Scripts emit a final-line JSON status:

print(json.dumps({"final_loss": 0.12, "final_metric": 0.91, "steps_used": 200}))

The grader parses the last {...} line, so any mid-run prints are fine.

docs.title: What lensml bench run does
docs.text:
For each fixture:

  1. Subprocess bug.py. Grade. Expected: ≥ one check fails.
  2. Apply fix.diff to bug.py → patched.py in a tmp dir.
  3. Subprocess patched.py. Grade. Expected: all checks pass.
  4. Record both as a FixtureRun (with bug_correctly_fails, fix_passes, overall_pass derived properties).

JSON cache (--cache PATH) lets you resume after Colab/Kaggle disconnects (plan §11 risk #6).

docs.title: The LLM-only baseline arm
docs.text:
lensml bench baseline --provider <name> runs every fixture through a single-shot prompt: "diagnose this and produce a unified diff." parse_diagnosis_class maps the LLM's prose to one of the 12 canonical detector slugs; parse_diff_from_response extracts the fenced diff … block. The diff is applied + graded the same way lensml bench run grades the canonical patch.

This is the credibility lynchpin (plan §6.3): if lensml-full doesn't beat single-shot LLM diagnosis on the same fixtures, the integration story doesn't hold up.

docs.title: Final report
docs.text:
lensml bench report --bench JSON --baseline JSON … --out DIR stitches arm-specific JSONs into one report.md with:

  • Headline (overall pass / fix-pass / bug-fails counts).
  • lensml-full vs LLM-only comparison table.
  • Confusion matrix per baseline arm (diagonal bolded).
  • Latency histogram across all arms (shared bucket edges).
  • Cost breakdown — every arm at $0.00.
  • Per-pathology aggregate.
  • Per-fixture pass/fail.
  • "What doesn't work yet" — fixtures whose patched failed.

docs.title: Adding a fixture
docs.text:
1. mkdir -p lensml/bench/fixtures/tiny/<class>/<idx>/.
  2. Write bug.py (must reliably fail at least one of the three checks).
  3. Write the fixed version manually, then generate the diff via difflib.unified_diff (see the regenerate fix.diff snippet in any of the existing fixtures' commit history).
  4. Write a grade.py shim (3 lines — see existing fixtures).
  5. Write meta.json with thresholds chosen so the bug fails and the fix passes.
  6. Run lensml bench run --pathology <class> to verify.

docs.title: Detectors & fix templates
docs.text: v1 ships eight stream-processing detectors and eight libcst-backed fix templates. Each detector is server-side: it consumes the broker's kind: "metric" events and emits kind: "anomaly" when it fires. Each fix template is a libcst.CSTTransformer that returns a FixResult (with a unified diff) and is idempotent on its own output.

docs.title: Detectors
docs.text:
slug signal severity persistence demo exploding_grad global grad-L2 > N× rolling mean (or NaN/Inf loss) critical streak ≥ 3 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ lr_too_high Δloss sign-flip rate > 0.6 over 50 steps warning cooldown 50 ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ dead_relu worst-module dead_fraction > 0.5 warning streak ≥ 5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐ missing_normalize first input_stats outside [-3, 3] / max > 50 / unsigned-range warning single-shot ⭐⭐⭐⭐ model_eval_not_called val event with model_training=True warning single-shot ⭐⭐⭐⭐ bad_init step-0 CE > 2× log(num_classes) warning single-shot ⭐⭐⭐ vanishing_grad min(per_layer_grad_l2) < 1e-7 AND max/min ratio > 100 warning streak ≥ 3 ⭐⭐⭐⭐ dataloader_bottleneck batch_wait_ms / step_time_ms > threshold warning streak ≥ 5 ⭐⭐⭐

Robustness contract: every observe() returns None for malformed events rather than raising. Detectors never publish — that's the runner's job.

docs.title: Fix templates
docs.text:
slug what it inserts idempotency AddGradientClipping clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=N) between loss.backward() and optimizer.step() skips if a clip call already sits between the two LowerLearningRate replaces the lr=… literal in the optimizer constructor replaces the value, doesn't duplicate ReplaceActivation nn.ReLU() → nn.LeakyReLU(0.01) (or any pair) guarded by class match AddNormalize appends transforms.Normalize(...) to a transforms.Compose([...]) list skips if Normalize already in the list InsertEvalMode wraps def validate(...) body with model.eval() … model.train() skips if first stmt is already <m>.eval() KaimingInit <model>.apply(lambda _m: ...kaiming_normal_...) after first construction applies to the first construction site only DataLoaderWorkers adds/replaces num_workers=4, pin_memory=True, persistent_workers=True on every DataLoader(...) replaces existing values; idempotent on its own output AddLRScheduler CosineAnnealingLR(optimizer, T_max=N) after optimizer + scheduler.step() after every optimizer.step() skips if a scheduler already follows the optimizer

Every transformer is parse-error tolerant: malformed source returns FixResult(applied=False, reason="parse error: …") rather than raising. The diff property uses difflib.unified_diff so the output applies cleanly via the bench grader's apply_diff().

docs.title: Adding a detector
docs.text:
1. Subclass lensml.detectors.base.Detector with name = "my_slug".
  2. Implement observe(event) -> Anomaly | None. Be robust to missing keys.
  3. Register it in lensml/server/app.py::_default_detectors (or pass via the detectors= kwarg of create_app).
  4. Add a unit test under tests/unit/test_detectors_my_slug.py.
  5. Add a tiny fixture under lensml/bench/fixtures/tiny/my_slug/0/ if the pathology has a tractable synthetic manifestation.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This page walks you from pip install to seeing the dashboard react to a real training run in about five minutes.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
lensml is not on PyPI yet, so install from GitHub:

pip install "git+https://github.com/rupeshbharambe24/lensml.git"                       # core
pip install "lensml[lightning] @ git+https://github.com/rupeshbharambe24/lensml.git"    # for Lightning callback
pip install "lensml[transformers] @ git+https://github.com/rupeshbharambe24/lensml.git" # for HF Trainer callback

docs.title: 2. Start the dashboard
docs.text:
lensml dashboard --db lensml.sqlite

That's a FastAPI server on :8000. The Next.js dashboard lives in dashboard/ of the repo — cd dashboard && pnpm install && pnpm dev to bring it up on :3000. The dashboard talks directly to :8000 over CORS (SSE doesn't survive Next's dev proxy).

docs.title: 3. Add lensml.watch() to your training loop
docs.text:
import lensml
import torch.optim as optim

model = MyNet()
optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.05)

handle = lensml.watch(model, optimizer, run_id="my-run")
try:
    for step in range(N):
        loss = train_step(model, optimizer)
        handle.log(loss=loss.item())     # optional — stream user metrics too
finally:
    handle.unwatch()

That's it. Hooks are installed on activation modules, optimizer.step is wrapped to capture pre-step gradients, and a 50ms-cadence telemetry stream goes to :8000. The dashboard's loss curve, grad-L2 trace, and agent reasoning pane update live.

docs.title: 4. Lightning
docs.text:
from lensml.integrations.lightning import LensmlCallback, lensml_resume_ckpt

trainer = pl.Trainer(callbacks=[LensmlCallback()], ...)
trainer.fit(model, datamodule, ckpt_path=lensml_resume_ckpt())

lensml_resume_ckpt() reads LENSML_RESUME so the supervisor's restart hand-off works automatically.

docs.title: 5. HuggingFace Trainer
docs.text:
from lensml.integrations.transformers import LensmlTrainerCallback, lensml_resume_ckpt

trainer = Trainer(model=..., args=..., callbacks=[LensmlTrainerCallback()])
trainer.train(resume_from_checkpoint=lensml_resume_ckpt())

HF's TrainerCallback is read-only, so lensml signals stop via control.should_training_stop = True. The callback then sys.exit(99) on on_train_end so the supervisor sees the sentinel.

docs.title: 6. Replay (for offline demos)
docs.text:
lensml replay --scenario exploding_grad --speed 2

Streams a deterministic recorded session through the dashboard. No GPU, no LLM, no flakiness — perfect for the live demo path.

docs.title: 7. Bench
docs.text:
lensml bench list                          # 8 packaged tiny fixtures
lensml bench run --out bench/results/$(date +%F)/
lensml bench baseline --provider groq --out bench/results/$(date +%F)/
lensml bench report \
    --bench bench/results/$(date +%F)/report.json \
    --baseline bench/results/$(date +%F)/baseline-groq.json \
    --out bench/results/$(date +%F)/

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: The 30-day FAR AWAY hackathon build (May–Jun 2026) ships v0.1. The implementation sequence file (here) records exactly what shipped on which day.

docs.title: v0.1 (FAR AWAY Round 1, June 7 2026)
docs.text:
• ✅ lensml.watch() for raw PyTorch with checkpoint resume + signal handling
  • ✅ Lightning callback (LensmlCallback)
  • ✅ HF Trainer callback (LensmlTrainerCallback)
  • ✅ All 8 v1 detectors
  • ✅ All 8 libcst fix templates
  • ✅ FastAPI server + SQLite event log + ZMQ bridge
  • ✅ Next.js dashboard with command palette + EN/JA i18n + privacy toggle
  • ✅ Replay mode + 3 deterministic demo scenarios
  • ✅ lensml-bench infrastructure + 8 tiny fixtures + LLM-only baseline arm
  • ⏳ Final benchmark report (numbers populate from external Colab/Kaggle runs)
  • ⏳ 90-second Round 1 video (recording infra in demo/; manual recording step)

docs.title: v0.2 (Q3 2026)
docs.text:
• Distributed-training support (DDP, FSDP, accelerate)
  • Medium and Large bench envs (DistilBERT/SST-2, GPT-2/WikiText-2)
  • Real Ollama integration for privacy mode (today's scaffolding is Plan-C: toggle + canned interaction; v0.2 wires the local model)
  • 4 stretch detectors fully shipped (label_leakage, train_val_contamination, mixed_precision_nan, lr_schedule_mismatch — lr_schedule_mismatch already has a tiny fixture)
  • Custom-detector API: lensml.detectors.register(my_detector)
  • Replay → mp4 export (today: live SSE only)

docs.title: v0.3
docs.text:
• Fine-tuned supervisor models for the diagnosis path (today: prompt-only)
  • Built-in pre-baked fixes for top-20 PyTorch antipatterns
  • Notebook (Jupyter) integration
